definition: A cultivated recognition that keeps the unsatisfactory side of conditioned experience in view.
notes: Use this record for the three-marks practice family when the dukkha-side recognition is being cultivated explicitly. In AN 10.60 the recognition appears in the more relational form anicce dukkhasaññā, so this entry should be heard as the governed family label for that practice rather than as permission to flatten dukkha back into suffering-language. The English follows the sanna record's default: recognition, not perception. Perception is discouraged here because readers take a perception to be a thing in its own right, something held and lasting, whereas sanna is the act of knowing the thing again -- re-cognizing it -- which is what this practice trains.

example_phrases.translation: recognition of dissatisfaction in the impermanent
example_phrases.notes: Canonical perception formula linking impermanence and dissatisfaction.
